=== G1 (BLOCKING IN EFFECT, NOT A DEFECT I CHARGE AGAINST THIS CODE): the lwb-lanes gate is RED on this PR right now, and my AGREE does not turn it green ===

MEASURED: `python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --base origin/main --head HEAD --pr 56` exits 1 at this head:
    FAIL: reviews/56/cloud-reviewer-b.json: verdict is 'DISAGREE', want 'AGREE'
    FAIL: f409184e2423: touches a shared path and has 0 independent review(s) in reviews/56/, needs 1
    FAIL: a55dbdf4b739: ... same

MECHANISM, measured not inferred. In _review_ok the VERDICT check runs BEFORE the staleness check. B's record reviewed adf2001; the reviewable head is now 80cdb57, so the record IS stale (head_sha.startswith('adf2001...') is False). But it never reaches the STALE branch: it is short-circuited by the verdict check, tagged rejection_kind ['other'], and 'other' rejections are appended to `errors` UNCONDITIONALLY and force independent_reviews to return False. I simulated adding a fresh, valid, independent AGREE at the current reviewable head alongside B's record: gate ok = False, still one error, the DISAGREE. So this record cannot unblock this PR.

WHY I DO NOT CHARGE IT AS A DEFECT OF THIS PR, having talked myself out of charging it. My first reading was that this PR fails to deliver its own headline property -- a55dbdf's subject is literally 'a stale review record must not veto an otherwise-sufficient set', and a stale DISAGREE is a stale review record that vetoes. On reflection that reading is wrong, and the opposite change would be worse: if a stale DISAGREE were downgradable, any author could nullify any reviewer's dissent by pushing one trivial commit to move the reviewable head. Vetoing on DISAGREE is INTENTIONAL and stated in the PR body, and the narrowing in c04be73 exists precisely because an earlier round over-widened and silenced dissent. This PR is also strictly better than main here: before it, EVERY rejection vetoed, stale AGREEs included. So this is a pre-existing, deliberate design tension that this PR improves without resolving -- not a regression it introduces.

BUT IT HAS NO CLEAN EXIT, AND THAT IS THE PART THAT NEEDS A DECISION. B's dissent is resolved ON THE MERITS -- its only blocking finding is fixed, which I verified independently below -- yet the gate cannot represent 'resolved'. The three available moves are: (a) delete B's record, which reviews/README.md calls falsifying evidence and which this repo has already done twice (PR #46's title is 'drop two unclearable stale DISAGREE records'); (b) change the check ordering, which reopens the push-to-clear-dissent hole above; (c) add an explicit, recorded supersession mechanism -- e.g. a record field naming the record it supersedes, or letting a DISAGREE be cleared only by a record from the SAME reviewer_id -- so dissent is withdrawn by its author rather than deleted by the code's author. I raise (c) as the shape that preserves both properties; I am not implementing it, because I review and do not author product code, and because this is an owner-level decision about the gate's semantics. Recording it explicitly so it is decided rather than discovered a fourth time.

=== F1 (B's BLOCKING FINDING): VERIFIED FIXED at 80cdb57 ===

B charged that _is_stale_only_rejection decided 'was this routine staleness' by substring-searching _review_ok's formatted error TEXT for the literal 'STALE', while every such message interpolates author-controlled values -- above all {rel}, the record's own filename, which reviews/README.md says explicitly does not matter. I did not take that on trust. I reproduced it against the PRE-FIX code (git show adf2001:scripts/lwb_lanes.py, run in isolation) and against this head, same script, five cases, each one non-AGREE record plus one fresh valid AGREE (REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_REVIEWS = 1, so the AGREE is sufficient alone), PR 56 so the identity rules apply:

  case                                                    pre-fix(adf2001)   at 80cdb57
  (a) CONTROL  DISAGREE, plain filename                   ok=False           ok=False
  (b) DISAGREE @ 'reviewer-B-NOT-STALE-really.json'       ok=True  BYPASS    ok=False  FIXED
  (c) collision @ 'collide-STALE.json'                    ok=True  BYPASS    ok=False  FIXED
  (d) collision, shared token itself 'STALEtok1'          ok=True  BYPASS    ok=False  FIXED
  (e) GENUINELY stale record (must still downgrade)       ok=True            ok=True   preserved

So B's finding was real and is now closed, and the fix did not over-narrow: (e) confirms genuine staleness is still downgraded. The control (a) is what makes (b)-(d) mean anything -- it is the same record differing only in author-controlled text.

THE FIX ITSELF, audited rather than assumed. _review_ok gained an out-parameter `rejection_kind`, a caller-owned list appended at the rejection branch that actually ran; _is_stale_only_rejection is deleted; independent_reviews tests `record_kind == ['stale']`. I checked mechanically that the tagging is total and unambiguous rather than trusting the diff: parsing the function body, there are 11 `return None` branches, ALL 11 tagged, with exactly 1 'stale' append and 10 'other'. No rejection path can return untagged.

I also checked the one way 'stale' could still be reached by a non-stale record: the STALE branch also fires on `not isinstance(reviewed_commit, str)` and `len(reviewed_commit) < 7`, which are malformedness, not staleness. That is NOT reachable in practice -- reviews/schema.json requires reviewed_commit with "pattern": "^[0-9a-f]{7,40}$" and _validate_against_schema runs earlier and tags 'other', so a missing, non-string or short reviewed_commit is rejected before the STALE branch. The 'stale' tag is reachable only by a genuine sha mismatch. I verified the schema file's actual contents rather than relying on README's description of it.

MUTATION PROBES on the fix, three, each reverted immediately, `git diff --quiet scripts/lwb_lanes.py` confirmed clean afterwards (it is):

       -> 5 failed, including test_independent_reviews_disagree_at_a_stale_named_path_still_fails
          and test_independent_reviews_self_review_collision_at_a_stale_named_path_still_fails
  (M2) over-narrow: the STALE branch tags 'other' instead of 'stale'
       -> 4 failed, including test_independent_reviews_genuinely_stale_at_a_stale_named_path_is_still_downgraded
          and test_independent_reviews_stale_is_downgraded_but_disagree_is_not_in_the_same_directory
  (M3) drop the 'other' tag from the DISAGREE branch entirely

M1 and M2 together show the new tests bite in BOTH directions, which is the thing this repository has shipped vacuous before. M3 is recorded as an observation, not a charge: an untagged rejection yields record_kind == [] which is != ['stale'], so it falls to the hard-error branch and VETOES -- the design is fail-closed, and a dropped 'other' tag can only ever make the gate stricter, never bypassable. But nothing in the suite would notice it, so the totality property I verified by parsing is held by no test.

=== F2 (B's non-blocking finding): CONFIRMED BY MY OWN MEASUREMENT, still stands ===
scripts/githooks/commit-msg's header says it 'moves the check to the moment the commit is written'. git does not run commit-msg for cherry-pick, and cherry-pick PRESERVES the original author. Measured in a throwaway repo outside this one (not committed anywhere), hook installed via core.hooksPath:
    poisoned commit authored 'LEAPWare-HQ <leapware@outlook.com>' on a side branch
    git cherry-pick <poisoned>  -> ACCEPTED, hook never ran, resulting author still 'LEAPWare-HQ <leapware@outlook.com>'
This is the exact defect class the hook exists to preempt, on the exact operation ('re-cut from the last good commit') the last five re-cuts used. Not blocking, and I verified WHY rather than asserting it: the CI backstop is real and non-vacuous, which I proved on real data rather than a synthetic case -- `scripts/lwb_check_commit_identity.py --base origin/main --head origin/lwb-recut-54-bad-identity` (PR #55's branch, whose tip e7827e58 is a real poisoned commit) exits 1 with 'FAIL: commit author not LEAPWare or an allow-listed bot: LEAPWare-HQ <leapware@outlook.com>'. So the hook is incomplete defence-in-depth, not a vacuous check. What stands is the header's unqualified claim: one sentence naming cherry-pick/rebase/am as uncovered would stop the next session trusting the hook through a re-cut.

=== NEAR-MISSES OF MY OWN, PRINTED AS REQUIRED ===
TWO.

FIRST, and it would have caused real damage. My instructions say to skip a PR whose reviews/<pr>/ holds a record naming the CURRENT HEAD SHA. I did that first, by REST, against head.sha -- and got 'ALL 13 OPEN PRs UNREVIEWED', every single record stale. I was one step from reviewing all 13 and filing 12 redundant records. The literal instruction is unsatisfiable: committing a review record advances the raw head past the sha that record names, so NO committed record can ever equal head.sha. The gate does not work that way -- resolve_reviewable_head skips record-only commits. Re-derived against the REVIEWABLE head, 12 of the 13 were already covered and only #56 was genuinely unreviewed. The cost of the literal reading is already visible in this repository: reviews/40/ holds SEVEN records and reviews/44/ FIVE, nearly all naming one single reviewable head. This is a defect in the reviewer routine's own instructions, not in any pull request, and I am recording it where the next run of that routine may see it.

SECOND, caught because B's record warned of it and I checked rather than assumed I was immune. My first coverage sweep computed every PR's reviewable head by importing ONE lwb_lanes.py for all 13. That is wrong: each PR's CI runs ITS OWN branch's checked-out lwb_lanes.py, and these branches disagree about what a reviewable head is (#54/#55/#56 carry the merge-aware commit_files; main does not; #45's resolve_reviewable_head has a different SIGNATURE entirely -- it takes pr_number, so the single-argument call I had written raised TypeError rather than returning a wrong answer). I redid the sweep loading each branch's own module separately, and handled #45's signature explicitly. The conclusion held -- 12 covered, only #56 unreviewed -- so nothing I filed depended on the error, but it held by luck rather than by method, and the general point stands and is worth writing down: during rollout of a change to resolve_reviewable_head, 'the reviewable head' is VERSION-DEPENDENT, so a reviewer must resolve it with the branch's own lanes.py, never with the newest one.
